newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: CRH spends 30.5mln punts on new developments.
newsitem.headline: CRH spends 30.5mln punts on new developments.

text.p: Irish building materials group CRH Plc said on Thursday that it recently spent 30.5 million Irish pounds on capital projects and acquisitions in mainland Europe and North America.
The recent investment follows acquistions and investments worth 405 million Irish pounds in 1996, CRH said in a statement.

"The acquisitions and investments announced today represent a continuation of the group's strategy of mid-sized deals which further strengthen existing market positions in our core businesses," CRH chief executive Don Godson said.

CRH said it had spent 25.5 million punts in mainland Europe. This involved expanding its DIY stores and building supplies depots in the Netherlands and acquiring Brakel, a Dutch manufacturer of glass rooflight structures and natural/smoke ventilation systems.
The acquisition of Brakel complements CRH's existing operations in the rooflight sector and gives the combined rooflight group annualised sales of more than 30 million punts.
CRH said this puts it in the top five players in the Northern European combined rooflight and natural ventilation market.
The company also bought Kleiwarenfabriek Echt, a Dutch extruded brick manufacturer.
In France, CRH acquired an 11 percent stake in Samse S.A., a publicly-quoted French builders merchants.
CRH said it spent 3.5 million acquiring the stake in Samse which operates 49 builders merchants outlets and 17 DIY stores.
In North America, CRH spent five million punts on acquisitions.

It acquired Synertech Moulded Products Inc, a polymer concrete company in Quebec, for three million punts and acquired certain assets of John Iafolla Company Inc, which owns asphalt plants and sand reserves in New Hampshire, for two million.
